W9b READ LIVE 2026-10-15 (call 1, w79w9b-u; call 6, w79w9b-l6): no status row on this board; the cells BB12.217, pill BB5.23 and the left button's BB5.23 (11930:47114); the right button's BB5.23 sits on the fill-less frame 11930:47119 whose ellipse 47120 has no effect, so it blurs nothing. Casey 2026-10-15 ruled the slot boards' blurs built on WebGL, masked to each cell, pill, button and the bar, flat fills where WebGL is off, and the same day, asked whether W9b's CPU blur of a WebGL readback kept it, answered "Real WebGL blur" (not accepted). Built so in main b12977017 "feat(slots): the boards' blurs run on Phaser's own Blur FX pipeline ...": every blur the ruling names (the background blurs under the plates and the load wash, the glow's and the streaks' layer blurs, the astronaut's inset) runs on Phaser's own Blur FX pipeline, its 13-tap shader driven across then down over WebGL textures, as many passes as half Figma's radius takes; the CPU blur and its readback are gone. It is baked once per scene build, not left running, so a plate shows the board as it stood when the scene was built. Two drop shadows from before the ruling stay 2D-canvas shadowBlur and draw soft on Canvas too: the wordmark's blurred drops (parts.ts) and the menu drawer's shadow (MenuScene.ts). On the Canvas renderer the plates stay flat, the glow keeps its stacked discs, the streaks their soft slabs and the astronaut its plain picture, pinned both ways. A WebGL context that is lost and comes back rebuilds every live scene, which bakes them again (main bdee1344c "fix(slots): a WebGL context that comes back rebuilds every live scene, so what the scenes bake on the GPU is drawn again ..."; in Chromium the glow, a cell patch and an inset read the same after a lose and restore as before, and black without the rebuild). Built: cells, pill and the left button: baked once per build, the board under the plates drawn into a WebGL texture (no readback) and blurred on the pipeline, each patch its sharp board with that blur laid over at the plate's fill alpha and kept inside the plate's own shape, laid between the plate's drops and its fill; a frame draws each patch as one textured quad and runs no pass (main b12977017 "feat(slots): the boards' blurs run on Phaser's own Blur FX pipeline ..."); the glow 152.967 across under its LB98.056, the boards' flat disc (main 2d8f9274b "feat(slots): the glow behind the grid draws as the boards draw it, a flat disc under a layer blur ...") blurred once on the pipeline at a quarter of its size and drawn as one picture (main b12977017 "feat(slots): the boards' blurs run on Phaser's own Blur FX pipeline ..."). The right button draws none, as its board. Measured in Chromium's WebGL (ANGLE, D3D11) with the engine's own modules bundled as they ship, on a test board: an edge blurred for sigma 2.6 / 6 / 9.1 / 18 measures 2.602 / 5.991 / 9.033 / 17.76 (no board asks past 17.07); each patch is opaque inside its plate's shape, empty outside, upright. Per frame nothing is blurred: 30 cell patches and the bar's drew in 2.4 ms against 2.4 ms with the plates flat (1200x675, RTX 5090). Per build, once when a scene starts and at each rotation, a whole Starbound desktop bake took 54-70 ms of main-thread time (the review's measure, page in front). Phones not measured. The game itself was not run in a browser. A cell's patch rides in its cell's container, so on a refill drop or the landing bounce it carries the board from the cell's resting place, 20% of it seen through the .8 plate (not checked in a browser).
